newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Eisai targets global expansion.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Eisai targets global expansion.

text.p: Japanese drug group Eisai Co Ltd said on Thursday that its global expansion was being spearheaded by Aricept, a drug for treating mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease.

In an interview with Reuters before Eisai officially announced the establishment of European operations in Britain, France and Germany, Eisai president and chief executive Haruo Naito said Eisai hoped to boost its international sales to 35 percent of the total from less than 10 percent at present, mostly in Asia.
"Japanese pharmaceutical circumstances are getting somewhat shaky, with a lot of uncertainties involved, so it is inevitable we should try to establish our operations overseas." he said.

Eisai, Japan's fourth biggest drug maker, is expected to be hard-hit by government-enforced price cuts of listed drugs in Japan in April. Analysts say 49 percent of Eisai's sales, which reached 273 billion yen last year, will be affected.

Alzheimer's drug Aricept, which will be marketed in the U.S, Britain, Germany and France jointly with Pfizer Inc, is the group's first product in Europe, apart from a hypertension drug licensed to Boehringer Mannheim.

Aricept has already been approved in the UK, and will be launched in Britain in April with a German launch expected later this year and roll-out in France planned for the middle of 1998. He said Italy and other markets "are also coming soon".
Eisai said on Thursday that sales of the drug in the U.S, where it was launched last month, are "more than we expected and selling very well". The product has not yet been launched in Japan.
"This is not the cure of the disease, but we expect an improvement in the cognitive disfunctions of patients such as memory loss," said Naito.

Naito said analysts' forecasts of peak sales of Aricept of $300 million in the U.S. and $160 million in Europe were cautious. "If we just count the number of Aricept-indicated patients we may have much larger figures," he said.
Naito said Eisai will invest $30 to 40 million in Europe over the next two to three years, and aims to achieve total drug sales of $300 million in the European Union within five years.

An Eisai proton pump inhibitor for treating peptic ulcers is currently being reviewed by British regulators, and drugs for septic shock and cancer are likely to follow. Noting the group's alliance with Pfizer on Aricept, Naito said "other products may need partners, but we would like to pick partners product by product".
Although Eisai is new to the European market, it has had a presence in Britain for five years through the Eisai London Research Laboratories based at University College, which employ 40 people.

Naito, who is the grandson of Eisai's founder, said the company had invested $50 million in the project, which is conducting research into neurological diseases, particularly multiple sclerosis and strokes.
"The progress here is very substantial and we are about to pick up several promising (drug) candidates created here," he said.
Eisai also has a European clinical development team of 25 at its new European headquarters in Hammersmith, west London, and a UK marketing team of 20.
